title: Microsoft Purview: run a Power Automate flow when a retention label's retention period ends (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: The briefing is supported by the roadmap, the supplied Microsoft notice and Microsoft Learn. Its configuration path, PowerShell call, licensing requirements and opt-in default are accurate; it also reports the conflicting government-cloud planning tables.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The flow must use the trigger When an item reaches the end of its retention period.
claims.quote: configure to use the trigger **When an item reaches the end of its retention period**.

claims.claim: Configuration creates a new retention label that retains the item for a specified period and runs the flow at its end.
claims.quote:
create a new retention label with the following configuration:
- Retain the item for a specified period of time
- At the end of the retention period, run the flow that you just created

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: A custom flow can send an email notification to a records manager.
claims.quote: Send an email notification to a records manager, or to the person who created or last modified a document

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: A custom flow can move a document to a SharePoint location used to store records centrally.
claims.quote: Move a document item to a SharePoint location where you centrally store records

claims.claim: The actions permit integration with other apps and services, providing a route for information about retained items to reach connected services.
claims.quote: The actions also allow integration with other apps and services.

claims.claim: By default the account creating the flow must also create the retention label.
claims.quote: By default, the account that creates the Power Automate flow must be the same account that creates the retention label.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: People with whom the flow is shared can also select it when creating a retention label.
claims.quote: If you share the flow in Power Automate, the people you share it with can also select the flow when they create a retention label.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The flow must be created using My flows in Power Automate.
claims.quote: In Power Automate, you must use the option **My flows** to create the flow.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Learn says to allow up to seven days after retention expiry for the flow to trigger.
claims.quote: you should allow up to seven days after the expiration period expires before the Power Automate flow is triggered.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Learn says to allow up to seven days for the compliance delete and relabel actions to complete.
claims.quote: For the Microsoft 365 compliance actions of delete and relabel, then allow up to seven days for these actions to complete.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Learn says to allow up to 14 days for Exchange compliance delete actions.
claims.quote: Specific for Exchange and the Microsoft 365 compliance actions of delete, allow up to 14 days.

claims.claim: The flow and compliance actions are queued and automatically retried after network or service delays.
claims.quote: Both the flow itself and the Microsoft 365 compliance actions in the flow are queued so that if there are any network or service delays, the flow and actions are automatically retried.

claims.claim: The principles of retention still apply, retaining an item for the longest period when retention policies conflict.
claims.quote: an item is always retained for the longest period if there is a conflict with one or more retention policies.

claims.claim: The flow is nevertheless triggered at the end of the label's own retention period.
claims.quote: However, the flow is always triggered at the end of the label's retention period.

claims.claim: Moving or renaming a file after the flow triggers but before compliance actions complete causes failure to find it unless the additional trigger-a-new-instance action is used.
claims.quote: This additional action is required for files that you move or rename after an instance of the flow is triggered but your specified compliance actions aren't completed. Without it, a renamed or moved file results in the flow failing because it can't find the file.

claims.claim: An existing retention label cannot be edited to add this end-of-retention flow configuration.
claims.quote: You must create a new retention label to run a flow at the end of the retention period. You can't edit an existing retention label for this configuration.

claims.claim: The same flow can be used by more than one retention label.
claims.quote: the same flow can be used by more than one retention label.

claims.claim: A flow in an environment type other than Default requires creating the label with PowerShell and FlowId.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; Scope; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Running this flow requires a Power Automate plan with premium connectors, separate from the Microsoft 365 compliance plan.
claims.quote: You must have a Power Automate plan that includes premium connectors, separate from your Microsoft 365 compliance plan.

claims.claim: The Purview service description lists Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5/E3/A3/G3/F3/F1/Business Premium among licences providing retention label creation rights.
claims.quote:
For retention label creation, the following licenses provide user rights:
- Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5/E3/A3/G3/F3/F1/Business Premium

claims.claim: The service description lists event-based retention start, disposition review, record marking and automatic relabelling as settings requiring more specific licences.
claims.quote:
- Start the retention period based on an event type
- Trigger a disposition review at the end of the retention period
- During the retention period mark items as a record or a regulatory record
- After the retention period, automatically change the retention label,

claims.claim: The service description's list of retention label creation settings needing specific licences does not name running a Power Automate flow.
claims.quote: Searched: Learn query 'site:learn.microsoft.com/purview retention label flow licensing Power Automate retention label creation'; searched the fetched Purview service description for 'retention label', 'Power Automate' and 'event-based'; read its label-creation settings list and retention-label-flow.

claims.claim: The roadmap record names no Power Automate plan, price or meter for this feature.
claims.quote: Initiate a Power Automate workflow when the item reaches the end of its retention period. For example, execute a complex disposition approval process or move the file to an archive.

claims.claim: The supplied Microsoft notice names no plan, price or meter for this feature.
claims.quote: No action is required. Review internal documentation and evaluate whether to use end-of-retention workflows.

claims.claim: Apply a retention label on the item is independent of the end-of-retention scenario.
claims.quote: This action is independent from this scenario that applies actions at the end of the retention period.

claims.claim: Apply a retention label on the item is equivalent to manually applying a retention label.
claims.quote: Instead, it's the equivalent to manually applying a retention label.

claims.claim: Apply a retention label on the item applies the label immediately.
claims.quote: The label is applied immediately.

claims.claim: The printed Purview route through Solutions, Records Management, File plan and retention label creation reaches Run a Power Automate flow, followed by Select a flow.
claims.quote:
On the **Define label settings** page, select **Retain items indefinitely or for a specific period** and specify the retention period.
On the **Choose what happens after the retention period** page, select **Run a Power Automate flow**, and then **Select a flow**

claims.claim: New-ComplianceTag -Name <label name> -FlowId <flow GUID> specifies the flow for a new label using documented parameters and an accepted GUID value.
claims.quote: The FlowId parameter specifies the Power Automate flow to run at the end of the retention period. A valid value for this parameter is the GUID value of the flow.

claims.claim: The licensing model is mixed, combining retention-label licensing with a separate Power Automate premium-connector plan requirement.
claims.quote: You must have a Power Automate plan that includes premium connectors, separate from your Microsoft 365 compliance plan.

claims.where: controls[0].ui: opening steps; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: In the Microsoft Purview portal, Solutions > Records Management > File plan > + Create a label > Retention label opens retention label creation.
claims.quote:
sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > **Solutions** > **Records Management** > **File plan**.
From the **File plan** page, select **+ Create a label** > **Retention label**

claims.claim: The flow-selection flyout lists automated cloud flows created by or shared with the current account that have the required end-of-retention trigger.
claims.quote: From the **Select a Power Automate flow** flyout pane, you'll see any automated cloud flows that you created (or somebody has shared with you) and that have the **When an item reaches the end of its retention period** trigger.

claims.claim: The resilience action can be added before the relabel and delete actions, as recommended by Learn.
claims.quote: Although optional, we recommend you always add the **Trigger a new instance of the flow if an item can't be located** action before **Relabel an item at the end of retention** and **Deletes an item at the end of retention**.
